data.title: Constitutive mTORC1 Activation in Skeletal Muscle Increases Inflammation but is not Sufficient to Impair Glucose Tolerance.
data.authors: Marchant ED; Kalenta H; Kilroe SP; May J; Martini WZ; Weldon KS et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Constitutive mTORC1 activation in mouse skeletal muscle (via GATOR1 complex KO) increases inflammatory markers but is not sufficient to impair glucose tolerance, indicating that additional metabolic inputs beyond muscle mTORC1 hyperactivation are required to drive glucose intolerance.
data.abstract_excerpt: Aberrant mTORC1 signaling in skeletal muscle has been implicated in aging and insulin resistance, however, it is not known whether chronic mTORC1 activation directly causes glucose intolerance. We tested the hypothesis that constitutive mTORC1 activation in mouse skeletal muscle impairs glucose homeostasis using tamoxifen-inducible, muscle-specific GATOR1 complex knockout.

extracted_findings.effect: Increased skeletal muscle inflammation without impairment of glucose tolerance
